```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Anchor here() to this page so paths work no matter where R starts
here::i_am("vital-statistics/index.qmd")

# House colours, ggplot2 theme, and the packages every post uses
source(here::here("R", "theme_cwr.R"))

library(ggiraph)   # interactive layers (geom_point_interactive) for cwr_interactive()

# ---- The data ------------------------------------------------------------
# Small tidy files written by R/02_clean_data.R, one per statistic. Every file
# has a `geo` column holding "Canada", "Ontario" or "Region" (the cleaning
# script types the word that cwr_region holds). It is made a factor in that
# order so the Region's line is drawn last, on top of the other two.
read_vs <- function(file) {
  read_csv(here("vital-statistics", "data", file), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(geo = factor(geo, levels = c("Canada", "Ontario", cwr_region)))
}

unemployment_rate <- read_vs("unemployment_rate.csv")
employment_change <- read_vs("employment_change.csv")
participation_rate <- read_vs("participation_rate.csv")
rates_by_age <- read_vs("rates_by_age.csv")
ei_beneficiaries <- read_vs("ei_beneficiaries.csv")
business_dynamics <- read_vs("business_dynamics.csv")
building_permits <- read_vs("building_permits.csv")
new_housing_price_index <- read_vs("new_housing_price_index.csv")
housing_starts <- read_vs("housing_starts.csv")
starts_intended_market <- read_vs("starts_intended_market.csv")
vacancy_rate <- read_vs("vacancy_rate.csv")
average_rent <- read_vs("average_rent.csv")
rent_change <- read_vs("rent_change.csv")
population_growth <- read_vs("population_growth.csv")
population_components <- read_vs("population_components.csv")
crime_severity <- read_vs("crime_severity.csv")
crime_rate <- read_vs("crime_rate.csv")

# When Statistics Canada last released each table the page uses (written by
# 02_clean_data.R from the metadata 01_get_data.R saves with the figures).
# updated() gives the latest release among a chart's tables, in words, for
# the "Updated" date in its subtitle: a chart drawn from several tables last
# changed when the newest of them came out. CMHC gives no release date, so
# its charts' subtitles have none.
releases <- read_csv(here("vital-statistics", "data", "releases.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()
updated <- function(...) {
  latest <- releases |>
    filter(table %in% c(...)) |>
    pull(released) |>
    max()
  # "September 4, 2026" (format()'s %e would pad the day with a space)
  str_c(format(latest, "%B "), day(latest), format(latest, ", %Y"))
}

# ---- One line chart, many times ------------------------------------------------
# Every chart on the page is the same picture: the Region in blue, Ontario in
# silver and Canada in red (or the Region alone), over five years. So the
# chart is built once, here, from the house ggline template (cwr-charts,
# lines.md), and each chunk below hands it its own data and adds its own
# labs() - the pattern the cwr-charts skill uses for tabs, so the charts
# cannot drift apart.
#
# A chunk renames its columns before calling vs_line():
#   x      the date (monthly series) or the year (annual ones)
#   y      the value
#   geo    the place
#   lower, upper  (optional) the Region's 95% confidence interval, drawn as a band
#
# The charts carry no line labels and no legend: one key at the top of the
# page names the three colours for every chart (the page-legend chunk).
# Hovering over a line shows the place, the period and the value instead.
# A chart whose lines are not the three places (the Region's business
# openings and closures) passes its own `colours` and names its lines on the
# chart with `label_lines = TRUE`, since the page's key does not cover them.

# Colours carry meaning (rule 2): blue the focus, red the main comparison,
# silver everyone else
vs_colours <- set_names(manual_3_colours, c("Canada", "Ontario", cwr_region))

vs_line <- function(plot_data,
                    y_labels = label_number(big.mark = ","),
                    limits = NULL,        # y limits, NA where the data decide
                    breaks = waiver(),    # y breaks
                    zero_line = FALSE,    # a darker line at zero, for values that go negative
                    x_labels = waiver(),
                    tip = label_number(big.mark = ","),   # the value, in words, for the tooltip
                    when = NULL,                          # the period, in words, for the tooltip
                    colours = vs_colours,                 # one colour per value of `geo`
                    label_lines = FALSE,                  # name each line on the chart
                    index = NULL) {                       # an index chart's base (100)
  dated <- inherits(pull(plot_data, x), "Date")
  banded <- "lower" %in% names(plot_data)
  if (is.null(when)) when <- if (dated) \(x) format(x, "%B %Y") else as.character

  # What the hover shows: the place in bold, the period, and the value. Each
  # point gets an id shared by its two hover layers below. A figure left out
  # as unreliable (NA) gets no hover point.
  hover_data <- plot_data |>
    filter(!is.na(y)) |>
    mutate(
      hover_id = str_c(geo, "-", x),
      tooltip = str_glue("<b>{geo}</b><br>{when(x)}<br>{tip(y)}")
    )

  # Room on the right for the axis numbers, which sit above their gridlines
  # and end where the gridlines end (the theme() block at the bottom). The
  # lines stop short of the panel's right edge by the same share of the x
  # range on every chart - 6% on a monthly chart, 7% on an annual one to
  # clear its end dots - which holds a number about three digits wide. A
  # chart whose numbers are wider rescales them (to thousands, say) rather
  # than widening the room; cwr_right_axis() at the bottom says when. (The phone
  # version moves the numbers outside the panel, where they need no room.)
  right_room <- if (dated) 0.06 else 0.07
  left_room <- if (dated) 0.02 else 0.06

  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = geo))

  # The Region's 95% confidence interval, where the source publishes one
  if (banded) {
    p <- p +
      geom_ribbon(
        data = filter(plot_data, geo == cwr_region),
        aes(x = x, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
        fill = dodgerblue, alpha = 0.15,
        inherit.aes = FALSE
      )
  }

  if (zero_line) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4)
  }

  # Line names (cwr-charts rule 3a), for a chart the page's key does not
  # cover. cwr_line_labels() sets each name's height from its own line and
  # finds a clear spot automatically, away from the other line; `span` is a
  # name's width in x units (days on a monthly chart) and `step` how finely
  # it searches. `label_height` and `gap` are sized for 3.2 mm text on a 5 in
  # chart, so the names clear the lines. Each name is in its own line's colour
  # (the `label` column holds the line's name, which the colour scale maps),
  # because two lines that cross every month leave no spot hugging one line
  # alone, and a grey name could belong to either.
  if (label_lines) {
    label_data <- cwr_line_labels(
      plot_data, x = x, y = y, group = geo,
      limits = limits, breaks = if (is.numeric(breaks)) breaks else NULL,
      label_height = 0.07,
      gap = if (dated) 0.02 else 0.03,
      span = if (dated) 330 else 0.6,
      step = if (dated) 15 else 0.1
    )
    if (dated) label_data <- mutate(label_data, x = as_date(x))
    p <- p +
      cwr_label(
        data = label_data,
        aes(x = x, y = y, label = label, fontface = fontface, vjust = vjust, colour = label),
        size = 3.2,
        hjust = 0.5,
        inherit.aes = FALSE
      )
  }

  # geom_line() breaks the line at a missing month, so a figure blanked as
  # unreliable leaves a gap rather than being bridged
  p <- p + geom_line(linewidth = 0.8)

  # Monthly series: a tick each January, labelled with the year, and a
  # minor tick each quarter. Annual series: a tick and a dot for each year,
  # since five points are few enough to mark, and no minor ticks - ggplot's
  # default would put one at each half-year, where there is no figure
  # (cwr-charts rule 4b: minor ticks only where the chart has data).
  if (dated) {
    x_min <- min(pull(plot_data, x))
    x_max <- max(pull(plot_data, x))
    p <- p +
      scale_x_date(
        # each January inside the data, so the room on the right never
        # sprouts a tick for a year with no data in it
        breaks = seq(ceiling_date(x_min, "year"), x_max, by = "1 year"),
        date_labels = "%Y",
        # each quarter's first month that is in the data, so no minor tick
        # falls where there is no figure (cwr-charts rule 4b)
        minor_breaks = keep(sort(unique(pull(plot_data, x))), \(d) month(d) %in% c(1, 4, 7, 10)),
        expand = expansion(mult = c(left_room, right_room))
      )
  } else {
    p <- p +
      geom_point(size = 1.8) +
      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = sort(unique(pull(plot_data, x))),
        minor_breaks = NULL,
        labels = x_labels,
        expand = expansion(mult = c(left_room, right_room))
      )
  }

  p <- p +
    # The hover layers (cwr-charts rule 3c). Small invisible dots that appear
    # on hover to mark the point...
    geom_point_interactive(
      data = hover_data, aes(data_id = hover_id),
      size = 2.5, alpha = 0
    ) +
    # ...under large invisible squares that catch the mouse anywhere near a
    # line and carry the tooltip. The squares go on top: a dot drawn over them
    # would take the mouse at the very point a reader aims for.
    geom_point_interactive(
      data = hover_data, aes(tooltip = tooltip, data_id = hover_id),
      shape = 15, size = 7, alpha = 0
    ) +

    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = limits,
      breaks = breaks,
      position = "right",
      labels = y_labels,
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))
    ) +

    # No legend: the key at the top of the page covers every chart, and a
    # chart with other lines names them on the chart
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +

    guides(x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = dated))

  # Right-axis numbers above their gridlines, ending where the gridlines end
  # (cwr-charts rule 6), with 0 labelled, or a zig-zag and a baseline stopping
  # at the last point when the axis does not reach zero (rule 6a).
  # cwr_right_axis() measures the numbers, and prints a
  # warning while the page renders if they are too wide to clear the ends of
  # the lines; that chart's chunk then rescales its axis (to thousands, say)
  # and says so in the subtitle. On an index chart (`index = 100`) the base
  # takes zero's place: its gridline is black and the axis is not cut.
  p <- p + cwr_right_axis(index = index)
  p
}

# ---- One bar chart, many times ------------------------------------------------
# The Region's own count of each component of population change, one bar per
# twelve months, from the house ggvertbar template (cwr-charts, bars.md) with
# the page's hover and axis habits. The chunk renames its columns to x (the
# year), y (the value) and geo (the Region), as for vs_line().
#
# The bars start at zero, so cwr_right_axis() lays the baseline on the zero
# gridline and labels 0 (rule 6a); where a count goes below zero, a darker
# line marks zero and the bars hang from it. The hover names the Region, the
# period and the value; the bar under the mouse does not change colour.
#
# The Region's net business openings use it too, a bar a month: a date `x`
# gets the monthly charts' axis (a year label each January, a minor tick each
# quarter), and `signed = TRUE` colours each bar by its sign - blue above
# zero, red below - instead of all blue. `colours` gives the two fills.
vs_bar <- function(plot_data,
                   y_labels = label_number(big.mark = ","),
                   breaks = waiver(),    # y breaks
                   x_labels = waiver(),
                   tip = label_number(big.mark = ","),
                   when = as.character,
                   signed = FALSE,       # red bars below zero
                   colours = c(positive = dodgerblue, negative = habsred)) {
  dated <- inherits(pull(plot_data, x), "Date")
  plot_data <- plot_data |>
    filter(!is.na(y)) |>
    mutate(
      sign = if_else(signed & y < 0, "negative", "positive"),
      hover_id = str_c(geo, "-", x),
      tooltip = str_glue("<b>{geo}</b><br>{when(x)}<br>{tip(y)}")
    )

  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_col_interactive(
      aes(tooltip = tooltip, data_id = hover_id, fill = sign),
      # a month's bar is 20 days wide, leaving a gap between months
      width = if (dated) 20 else 0.7
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colours, guide = "none")

  if (any(pull(plot_data, y) < 0)) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4)
  }

  if (dated) {
    # As vs_line()'s monthly charts: a label each January inside the data,
    # and minor ticks only on the quarters' first months that have a bar
    # (cwr-charts rule 4b)
    x_min <- min(pull(plot_data, x))
    x_max <- max(pull(plot_data, x))
    p <- p +
      scale_x_date(
        breaks = seq(ceiling_date(x_min, "year"), x_max, by = "1 year"),
        date_labels = "%Y",
        minor_breaks = keep(sort(unique(pull(plot_data, x))), \(d) month(d) %in% c(1, 4, 7, 10)),
        expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.07))
      )
  } else {
    p <- p +
      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = sort(unique(pull(plot_data, x))),
        minor_breaks = NULL,
        labels = x_labels,
        # the same room on the right as the page's annual line charts, for the
        # axis numbers
        expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.07))
      )
  }

  p +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = breaks,
      position = "right",
      labels = y_labels,
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))
    ) +
    guides(x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = dated)) +
    # Numbers right-aligned with the gridlines, 0 labelled (rules 6, 6a)
    cwr_right_axis()
}

# ---- Alt text ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Every chart's alt text ends with its latest figures, worked out from the
# data it draws so they cannot go stale when the page is refreshed. `fmt`
# turns a number into words ("5.8%"); `when` names the latest period.
vs_latest <- function(plot_data, fmt, when = \(x) format(x, "%B %Y")) {
  latest <- plot_data |>
    filter(!is.na(y)) |>
    group_by(geo) |>
    slice_max(x, n = 1) |>
    ungroup()
  place_names <- c("Canada" = "Canada", "Ontario" = "Ontario") |> c(set_names("Waterloo Region", cwr_region))
  figures <- latest |>
    arrange(desc(geo)) |>
    mutate(text = str_c(place_names[as.character(geo)], " ", fmt(y))) |>
    pull(text)
  str_glue("In {when(max(pull(latest, x)))}: {str_flatten_comma(figures, ', and ')}.")
}

# The first and last periods on a chart, for the start of its alt text
vs_span <- function(plot_data, when = \(x) format(x, "%B %Y")) {
  str_glue("from {when(min(pull(plot_data, x)))} to {when(max(pull(plot_data, x)))}")
}

# The Region, in words, for alt text: most series are for the census
# metropolitan area rather than the Region itself
cma_words <- "Waterloo Region (the Kitchener - Cambridge - Waterloo census metropolitan area)"

# An annual period that runs July to June, written "2024/25"
year_span <- \(year) str_c(year, "/", str_sub(year + 1, 3, 4))

# Number formats shared by several charts' tooltips and alt text
percent_1 <- label_percent(accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1)
percent_change <- label_percent(accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1, style_positive = "plus")

# The stock notes, written out once here because many charts carry them
# (cwr-charts rule 1d); edit the wording here and every chart follows
# Most figures are for the Kitchener - Cambridge - Waterloo CMA, which leaves
# out Wellesley Township; the note above the charts says so once for the
# page. The charts that are for the whole Region say so with this note.
whole_region_note <- str_glue("{cwr_region} includes Wellesley Township")
lfs_note <- "Estimates from the Labour Force Survey, a monthly sample of about 65,000 households"
rms_note <- "Estimates from CMHC's October Rental Market Survey, a sample of privately initiated rental buildings of three or more units"
centres_note <- "Ontario and Canada: centres of 10,000 people or more, the areas CMHC counts every month"
```

<!-- Opening paragraph: what the page is and how often it is refreshed. -->

```{r}
#| label: page-legend
#| output: asis

# One key for the whole page, in place of a legend or line labels on each
# chart: every chart draws the same three places in the same three colours
# (a chart of the Region alone draws only its blue line). The colours come
# from vs_colours, so the key cannot drift from the charts. prismatic turns
# an R colour name such as "dodgerblue4", which a browser does not know, into
# its hex code.
legend_key <- function(place, colour) {
  str_glue(
    '<span style="display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.45em; margin-right: 1.5em;">',
    '<span style="display: inline-block; width: 1.8em; height: 3px; background: {as.character(prismatic::color(colour))};"></span>',
    '{place}</span>'
  )
}

cat(
  '<div class="vs-legend" style="margin: 0.5em 0 1.5em;">',
  '<p style="margin-bottom: 0.25em;">',
  # the Region first, as on the charts
  str_flatten(map2_chr(rev(names(vs_colours)), rev(vs_colours), legend_key)),
  '</p>',
  '<p style="font-size: 0.9em; color: #555;">This legend applies to all charts on this page.</p>',
  '</div>',
  sep = ""
)
```

<!-- A note on the Region's figures for the whole page; Greg's to reword. -->

Region figures exclude Wellesley Township because it is not part of the Kitchener - Cambridge - Waterloo census metropolitan area (CMA).

## Labour market

### Unemployment rate

::: panel-tabset
### Overall

```{r}
#| label: unemployment-rate

plot_data <- unemployment_rate |>
  rename(x = date, y = percent, lower = percent_lower, upper = percent_upper)

p <- vs_line(plot_data, y_labels = label_number(accuracy = 1), tip = percent_1) +
  labs(
    title = "Unemployment rate",                                      # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = str_glue("Per cent of the labour force · Monthly · Updated {updated('14-10-0459-01')}"),
    caption = cwr_caption(
      "Statistics Canada Table 14-10-0459-01",
      credit = TRUE,   # the band is worked out here from the published standard errors
      notes = c(
        str_glue("The band shows the {cwr_region}'s 95% confidence interval"),
        "Three-month moving averages, adjusted for the seasons",
        lfs_note
      )
    )
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-unemployment-rate",
  alt = str_glue(
    "Line chart of the unemployment rate, a three-month moving average adjusted for the seasons, ",
    "{vs_span(plot_data)}, for {cma_words}, Ontario and Canada, with a band showing the Region's ",
    "95% confidence interval. {vs_latest(plot_data, percent_1)}"
  ),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5
)
```

### 15 to 24

```{r}
#| label: unemployment-rate-15-24

# Shared by the six age tabs, three for the unemployment rate and three for
# the participation rate. The CMA publishes these by age only without
# seasonal adjustment, so, unlike the Overall tabs, every line rises and falls
# with the seasons. Ten-year age groups are not published for the CMA; these
# three cover 15 to 64. unpublished_note() names any month Statistics Canada
# rates too unreliable to publish (F), which leaves a gap in the Region's line,
# and returns nothing when there is none, which cwr_caption() treats as no note.
by_age <- function(which_measure, which_age) {
  rates_by_age |>
    filter(measure == which_measure, age == which_age) |>
    rename(x = date, y = percent)
}
unpublished_note <- function(plot_data) {
  blanked <- plot_data |>
    filter(geo == cwr_region, is.na(y)) |>
    pull(x) |>
    format("%B %Y")
  if (length(blanked) > 0) {
    str_glue("{cwr_region} not shown for {str_flatten_comma(blanked, ' and ')}: too unreliable to be published")
  }
}
age_caption <- function(plot_data) {
  cwr_caption(
    c("Statistics Canada Tables 14-10-0458-01", "14-10-0017-01"),
    credit = TRUE,   # Ontario's and Canada's three-month averages are worked out here
    notes = c(
      unpublished_note(plot_data),
      "Three-month moving averages, not adjusted for the seasons",
      "No confidence intervals are published for these figures; rates close together may differ only by sampling error",
      lfs_note
    )
  )
}
age_alt <- function(plot_data, rate_words, age_words) {
  str_glue(
    "Line chart of the {rate_words} of people aged {age_words}, a three-month moving average not ",
    "adjusted for the seasons, {vs_span(plot_data)}, for {cma_words}, Ontario and Canada. ",
    "{vs_latest(plot_data, percent_1)}"
  )
}

plot_data <- by_age("Unemployment rate", "15 to 24 years")

p <- vs_line(plot_data, y_labels = label_number(accuracy = 1), tip = percent_1) +
  labs(
    title = "Unemployment rate of people aged 15 to 24",              # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = str_glue("Per cent of the labour force aged 15 to 24 · Monthly · Updated {updated('14-10-0458-01', '14-10-0017-01')}"),
    caption = age_caption(plot_data)
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-unemployment-rate-15-24",
  alt = age_alt(plot_data, "unemployment rate", "15 to 24"),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5
)
```

### 15 to 24

```{r}
#| label: participation-rate-15-24

plot_data <- by_age("Participation rate", "15 to 24 years")

p <- vs_line(plot_data, y_labels = label_number(accuracy = 1), tip = percent_1) +
```

## Business and construction

### Business openings and closures

::: panel-tabset
### Region

```{r}
#| label: business-region

# Shared by the three business charts: the Region's net openings (openings
# less closures), then each per 100 active businesses beside Ontario and Canada.
# business_gap_note() names any months left blank because Statistics Canada
# flags a figure behind them for use with caution (E), and returns nothing
# when there are none, which cwr_caption() treats as no note.
business_rate <- function(which) {
  business_dynamics |>
    filter(measure == which) |>
    rename(x = date, y = percent)
}
business_gap_note <- function(plot_data) {
  blanked <- plot_data |>
    filter(geo == cwr_region, is.na(y)) |>
    pull(x) |>
    format("%B %Y")
  if (length(blanked) > 0) {
    str_glue("{cwr_region} not shown for {str_flatten_comma(blanked, ' and ')}: Statistics Canada flags a figure it is worked out from for use with caution")
  }
}
business_rate_fmt <- label_number(accuracy = 0.01)

# The Region's net openings each month: businesses opening less businesses
# closing, as bars - light blue in a month with more openings, light red in one
# with more closures - with the 12-month moving average over them as a black
# line. Neither count is flagged, so no month is missing. The hover names the
# Region, the month and the net figure, signed.
net_fmt <- label_number(big.mark = ",", style_positive = "plus")

plot_data <- business_dynamics |>
  filter(geo == cwr_region) |>
  select(geo, date, measure, businesses) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = businesses) |>
  mutate(y = Openings - Closures) |>
  rename(x = date) |>
  arrange(x) |>
  # The average of each month and the eleven before it. slider::slide_dbl()
  # runs mean() over that window; `.complete = TRUE` leaves the first eleven
  # months without one (NA), since they have no full year behind them.
  mutate(average = slider::slide_dbl(y, mean, .before = 11, .complete = TRUE))

# A key for the average line, inside the plot: a short black line and its
# name, a fifth of the way along the months and four-fifths of the way up to
# the tallest bar, where the bars (tallest at the very start) leave room. Its
# spot comes from the data, so it moves with them; if a new month ever puts a
# tall bar under it, move `key_x` or `key_y`.
x_range <- range(pull(plot_data, x))
key_x <- x_range[1] + 0.2 * as.numeric(diff(x_range))
key_y <- 0.8 * max(pull(plot_data, y))

p <- vs_bar(plot_data, y_labels = label_number(big.mark = ","), tip = net_fmt,
            when = \(x) format(x, "%B %Y"), signed = TRUE,
            colours = c(positive = dodgerblue50, negative = habsred50)) +
  # The 12-month moving average, over the bars (from the first full year on)
  geom_line(
    data = filter(plot_data, !is.na(average)),
    aes(x = x, y = average),
    colour = "black",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  annotate("segment", x = key_x, xend = key_x + 90, y = key_y, yend = key_y,
           colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  cwr_label(
    data = tibble(x = key_x + 110, y = key_y, label = "12-month moving average"),
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
    colour = "black", size = 3.2, hjust = 0,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Net business openings in the Region",                    # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = str_glue("Businesses opening less businesses closing · Monthly · Updated {updated('33-10-0270-01')}"),
    caption = cwr_caption(
      "Statistics Canada Table 33-10-0270-01",
      credit = TRUE   # openings less closures, and its average, are worked out here
    )
  )

months_net_closing <- plot_data |>
  filter(y < 0) |>
  nrow()

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-business-region",
  alt = str_glue(
    "Bar chart of the number of businesses opening less the number closing each month, seasonally ",
    "adjusted, {vs_span(plot_data)}, in {cma_words}. More businesses closed than opened in ",
    "{months_net_closing} of the {nrow(plot_data)} months. A line shows the 12-month moving average. ",
    "In {format(max(pull(plot_data, x)), '%B %Y')}: {net_fmt(last(pull(plot_data, y)))}, and a ",
    "12-month average of {net_fmt(round(last(pull(plot_data, average)), 1))} a month."
  ),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5
)
```

```{r}
# Shared by the three intended-market tabs: one market's share of the starts
# over the past 12 months, with the same notes on each
market_share <- function(which) {
  starts_intended_market |>
    filter(intended_market == which) |>
    rename(x = date, y = percent)
}
market_caption <- cwr_caption(
  "CMHC Starts and Completions Survey",
  credit = TRUE,   # the 12-month shares are worked out here
  notes = c(
    centres_note,
    "Co-operatives are not shown, so the three shares do not quite add to 100"
  )
)
market_fmt <- label_percent(accuracy = 1, scale = 1)
market_alt <- function(plot_data, market_words) {
  str_glue(
    "Line chart of the percentage of housing starts over the past 12 months intended for the ",
    "{market_words} market, {vs_span(plot_data)}, for {cma_words}, and for Ontario's and ",
    "Canada's centres of 10,000 people or more. {vs_latest(plot_data, market_fmt)}"
  )
}

plot_data <- market_share("Rental")

p <- vs_line(plot_data, y_labels = label_number(accuracy = 1), tip = market_fmt) +
  labs(
    title = "Rental share of housing starts over the past 12 months",   # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = "Per cent of housing starts · Monthly",
    caption = market_caption
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-starts-rental-share",
  alt = market_alt(plot_data, "rental"),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5
)
```

## Rental market

### Vacancy rate

::: panel-tabset
### All units

```{r}
#| label: vacancy-rate

# Shared by the twelve rental charts: three measures from CMHC's October
# Rental Market Survey - the vacancy rate, the average rent and the
# same-sample rent change - each for all units and then by unit size, one
# size a tab. A size is charted only where the Region has at least four usable
# figures of the five (Greg, 2026-09-26), which leaves out the studio vacancy
# rate and the studio and 3+ bedroom rent changes; rms_size() prints a warning
# while the page renders if a refresh leaves a charted size below that.
october <- \(x) str_c("October ", x)

# How each unit size is named in alt text; the data use CMHC's own names
unit_words <- c(
  "Total" = "all units",
  "Studio" = "studios",
  "1 Bedroom" = "one-bedroom units",
  "2 Bedroom" = "two-bedroom units",
  "3 Bedroom +" = "units with three or more bedrooms"
)

rms_size <- function(data, size) {
  plot_data <- data |>
    filter(bedroom_type == size) |>
    rename(x = year, y = value)
  usable <- plot_data |>
    filter(geo == cwr_region, !is.na(y)) |>
    nrow()
  if (usable < 4) {
    cat("WARNING - rental charts: the Region has only ", usable, " usable figures for ", size,
        " (", deparse(substitute(data)), "); the page charts a unit size only with four or more.\n",
        sep = "", file = stderr())
  }
  plot_data
}

# Names each October the Region's line skips, and why: CMHC rated the figure
# "Fair (Use with Caution)", which the site never uses (it is blanked in
# 02_clean_data.R), or did not publish it. Returns nothing when there is no
# gap, which cwr_caption() treats as no note.
rms_gap_note <- function(plot_data) {
  gaps <- plot_data |>
    filter(geo == cwr_region, is.na(y)) |>
    mutate(why = if_else(is.na(quality), "not published", "rated for use with caution"))
  if (nrow(gaps) > 0) {
    reasons <- gaps |>
      summarise(years = str_flatten_comma(october(x), " and "), .by = why) |>
      mutate(text = str_c(years, " (", why, ")")) |>
      pull(text)
    str_glue("{cwr_region} not shown for {str_flatten(reasons, '; ')}: CMHC's sample of these units is small")
  }
}

rms_caption <- function(plot_data) {
  cwr_caption("CMHC Rental Market Survey", notes = c(rms_gap_note(plot_data), rms_note))
}

rms_alt <- function(plot_data, size, measure_words, fmt) {
  str_glue(
    "Line chart of {measure_words} {unit_words[[size]]} in purpose-built rental apartments and ",
    "rows each October, {vs_span(plot_data, as.character)}, for {cma_words}, Ontario and Canada. ",
    "{vs_latest(plot_data, fmt, october)}"
  )
}

# The axis numbers are rounded finely (0.1, or $10 on the rent charts), since
# the gridlines can fall on halves or quarters; cwr_right_axis() then drops
# the zeros the numbers all share, so whole steps still read "1, 2, 3".
# The rent changes start their axis at zero unless one goes below it
from_zero <- \(plot_data) c(min(0, pull(plot_data, y), na.rm = TRUE), NA)
dollars_1 <- label_dollar(accuracy = 1)

plot_data <- rms_size(vacancy_rate, "Total")

p <- vs_line(plot_data, y_labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.1), limits = c(0, NA),
             tip = percent_1, when = october) +
  labs(
    title = "Rental vacancy rate, all units",   # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = "Per cent of rental units · Annual, each October",
    caption = rms_caption(plot_data)
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-vacancy-rate",
  alt = rms_alt(plot_data, "Total", "the vacancy rate in", percent_1),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5
)
```

### Components of population change

::: panel-tabset
### Natural increase: Region

```{r}
#| label: components-natural-region

# Shared by the ten component charts: for each component, the Region's
# number of people over the twelve months from July to June, as bars, then
# the same per 1,000 people beside Ontario and Canada, as lines. These are the
# whole Region (the census-division table), so they carry whole_region_note.
components_people <- function(which) {
  population_components |>
    filter(geo == cwr_region, component == which) |>
    rename(x = year, y = people)
}
components_per_1000 <- function(which) {
  population_components |>
    filter(component == which) |>
    rename(x = year, y = per_1000)
}
people_fmt <- label_number(big.mark = ",", style_positive = "plus")
per_1000_fmt <- label_number(accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus")
components_people_alt <- function(plot_data, component_words) {
  str_glue(
    "Bar chart of {component_words} in Waterloo Region, in people, for each twelve months from ",
    "July to June, {vs_span(plot_data, year_span)}. {vs_latest(plot_data, people_fmt, year_span)}"
  )
}
components_rate_alt <- function(plot_data, component_words, places = "Waterloo Region, Ontario and Canada") {
  str_glue(
    "Line chart of {component_words} per 1,000 people, for each twelve months from July to June, ",
    "{vs_span(plot_data, year_span)}, for {places}. ",
    "{vs_latest(plot_data, per_1000_fmt, year_span)}"
  )
}
# On a phone, five "2020/21" labels do not fit across: every other one is kept
components_phone <- list(scale_x_continuous(
  breaks = sort(unique(pull(population_components, year)))[c(TRUE, FALSE)],
  labels = year_span,
  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.1))
))

plot_data <- components_people("Natural increase")

# The axis is in thousands of people
p <- vs_bar(plot_data, y_labels = label_number(scale = 1e-3, accuracy = 0.1), x_labels = year_span,
            tip = people_fmt, when = year_span) +
  labs(
    title = "Natural increase in the Region",                         # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = str_glue("Thousands of people · Annual, July to June · Updated {updated('17-10-0153-01')}"),
    caption = cwr_caption(
      "Statistics Canada Table 17-10-0153-01",
      credit = TRUE,   # births less deaths is worked out here
      notes = whole_region_note
    )
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-components-natural-region",
  alt = components_people_alt(plot_data, "natural increase (births less deaths)"),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5, phone = components_phone
)
```

```{r}
# The axis is in thousands of people, a gridline every thousand
p <- vs_bar(plot_data, y_labels = label_number(scale = 1e-3, accuracy = 1), breaks = breaks_width(1000),
            x_labels = year_span, tip = people_fmt, when = year_span) +
  labs(
    title = "Net interprovincial migration, Region",                  # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = str_glue("Thousands of people · Annual, July to June · Updated {updated('17-10-0153-01')}"),
    caption = cwr_caption("Statistics Canada Table 17-10-0153-01", notes = whole_region_note)
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-components-interprovincial-region",
  alt = components_people_alt(plot_data, "net interprovincial migration (moves from other provinces less moves to them)"),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5, phone = components_phone
)
```

## Crime

::: panel-tabset
### Overall: Crime Severity Index

```{r}
#| label: crime-severity

# Shared by the six crime charts: for all crime, violent crime and non-violent
# crime, the Crime Severity Index and then the number of police-reported
# incidents per 100,000 people. Not the stock CMA note: crime figures are
# compiled from police services, and both tables' footnotes (52 and 110) say
# the policing CMA may not match the census one (see the README's Reliability
# table).
crime_index <- function(which) {
  crime_severity |>
    filter(index == which) |>
    rename(x = year, y = value)
}
crime_per_100k <- function(which) {
  crime_rate |>
    filter(kind == which) |>
    rename(x = year, y = per_100k)
}
crime_note <- str_glue("{cwr_region}: the Kitchener - Cambridge - Waterloo CMA as policed, whose boundary Statistics Canada says may not match the census CMA")
crime_index_caption <- cwr_caption("Statistics Canada Table 35-10-0026-01", notes = crime_note)
crime_rate_caption <- cwr_caption("Statistics Canada Table 35-10-0177-01", notes = crime_note)
crime_places <- str_c(
  "Waterloo Region (the Kitchener - Cambridge - Waterloo census metropolitan area as policed), ",
  "Ontario and Canada"
)
index_fmt <- label_number(accuracy = 0.1)
rate_fmt <- label_number(accuracy = 1, big.mark = ",")
crime_index_alt <- function(plot_data, index_words) {
  str_glue(
    "Line chart of the {index_words}, 2006 = 100, {vs_span(plot_data, as.character)}, for ",
    "{crime_places}. {vs_latest(plot_data, index_fmt, as.character)}"
  )
}
crime_rate_alt <- function(plot_data, kind_words) {
  str_glue(
    "Line chart of {kind_words} incidents reported to police per 100,000 people, ",
    "{vs_span(plot_data, as.character)}, for {crime_places}. ",
    "{vs_latest(plot_data, rate_fmt, as.character)}"
  )
}

plot_data <- crime_index("All crime")

p <- vs_line(plot_data, y_labels = label_number(accuracy = 1), index = 100, tip = index_fmt) +
  labs(
    title = "Crime Severity Index",                                   # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = str_glue("Index, 2006 = 100 · Annual · Updated {updated('35-10-0026-01')}"),
    caption = crime_index_caption
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-crime-severity",
  alt = crime_index_alt(plot_data, "Crime Severity Index"),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5
)
```

### Overall: incidents per 100,000 people

```{r}

  labs(
    title = "Police-reported incidents per 100,000 people",           # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = str_glue("Thousands of incidents per 100,000 people · Annual · Updated {updated('35-10-0177-01')}"),
    caption = crime_rate_caption
  )

cwr_interactive(
  p, "fig-crime-rate",
  alt = crime_rate_alt(plot_data, "all criminal"),
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5
)
```
